raw_answer_text:
A1: The unicast routing table (RIB).
A2: The packet's source address is used as the lookup key.
A3: It also tells the router the expected upstream (incoming) interface toward that source, i.e., the next-hop/outgoing interface used to reach it.
A4: It compares that interface to the interface on which the packet actually arrived.
A5: The router first looks up the route back toward the source, then compares it to the arrival interface.
A6: It passes when the interface matches the one the packet arrived on; the router then forwards/accepts the packet for multicast forwarding.
A7: It fails when the interface does not match the arrival interface; the router drops the packet.
A8: Because it checks the path back toward where the packet came from (its source) rather than where it's going, reversing the normal forwarding lookup direction.
